what_it_is: Founder-led, long-hold water services HoldCo (founded 2019/2020 by Peter Brooks and Michael Warady) that has bought ~17 small regional businesses since 2021. Two divisions: Sylmar Water Treatment (industrial/commercial cooling, boiler, closed-loop, Legionella and process-water chemical treatment programs, plus two custom chemical blenders ETI and ProChem, and RO/UF/ClO2 equipment) and Sylmar Utilities Group (water-well drilling/rehab and pump services for Southern California utilities and agriculture).
bluntly: A roll-up of regional HVAC/industrial water treaters, the kind that compete with Chem-Aqua, ChemTreat and local independents. It also owns a small toll/private-label blending business (ETI) that supplies other treaters. About a quarter to a third of revenue is well-drilling and pump contracting (General Pump, Water Well Solutions, Legend, Airburst). That work is water infrastructure services, not chemicals. On a strict basis, water treatment chemicals and service make up about 67% of pro forma revenue.

pe_sponsor: Not a traditional PE fund. Equity: Westerly Group (anchor investor, 2020), with M2O and Novidam also listed as investors (PitchBook). Debt: Balance Point Capital (2022, junior/sub debt); Manulife | Comvest Credit Partners ($130M senior secured refinancing, Feb 2026).

prior_owners: Each add-on was founder/family-owned before acquisition (e.g., EAI 1986 founders; ETI founders incl. Robert Keeler; Tower Water, Baskin family; Butler Water Corrections, founded 1938).
total_revenue_basis: Estimate. ZoomInfo lists $77.3M (last-resort source, likely pre-2026 add-ons). Built up from brand-level estimates: water treatment brands owned through 2025 are ~$62M. The 2026 add-ons add ~$17M (Tower ~$11M, since it has 50+ employees and is described as the 'largest acquisition to date'; Aquatrol ~$3M; Butler ~$2M; Atlantic ~$1M). Equipment is ~$7M and utility (pump/well) services are ~$30M (prior 30% share). No company-disclosed revenue.
ebitda_basis: Estimate. Manulife|Comvest led a $130M senior secured facility in Feb 2026 to refinance debt and fund acquisitions. Assume ~$90-110M funded at typical lower-middle-market leverage of ~4.5-5.5x, which implies ~$18-22M EBITDA. That is consistent with an ~18% margin for route-based water treatment service plus blending. The prior estimate of ~$24M is revised down slightly. No reported EBITDA was found.

profile_md:
## Sylmar Group: investor profile

**Overview.** Sylmar Group is a Los Angeles-based, founder-led water services holding company. It was formed in 2019-2020 by Peter Brooks (CEO; ex-US Marine infantry officer, HBS) and Michael Warady (President; Yale SOM). Sylmar presents itself as a "neither PE fund nor strategic" permanent-capital buyer of legacy, founder-owned water businesses. Since its first acquisition in 2021 it has assembled about 17 businesses in two divisions:
- **Sylmar Water Treatment** is the industrial/commercial chemical treatment and service business and the bulk of value.
- **Sylmar Utilities Group** does water-well drilling, rehabilitation and pump services, mainly for Southern California utilities and agriculture.

The company markets "8 brands across 30+ states." We estimate 2026 pro forma revenue at about $112M and EBITDA at about $20M; neither is disclosed. Water-treatment chemicals and service make up about two-thirds of the total.

**History & ownership.** Westerly Group (a Yale-alumni investment firm) anchored the 2020 equity raise and called it its "largest investment to date." PitchBook also lists M2O and Novidam as equity investors. Balance Point Capital provided debt in November 2022 to fund the first two platforms: EAI Water (Walnut, CA, founded 1986) and General Pump Company (San Dimas/Camarillo, CA). In February 2026, Manulife | Comvest Credit Partners was sole lender and agent on a $130M senior secured facility that refinanced prior debt and funds more M&A. In June 2026 Sylmar hired CFO Mark Hardee and appointed Melinda Sych (President) and Kevin Donaldson (COO) to run Sylmar Water Treatment. That is a professionalization step typical ahead of a larger recap.

**Products & chemistries.** The core business is route-based service chemistry: cooling-tower, boiler/steam and closed-loop programs, Legionella water-management plans, softening, RO pre-treatment, and wastewater and reuse treatment. Sylmar has vertically integrated into blending:
- **Eastern Technologies Inc.** (Morgantown, PA, 1986; acquired Dec 2024) is a custom/private-label blender that supplies independent water treaters. It hosts an annual distributor summit and launched the COOLGARD non-phosphorus cooling line in 2026.
- **ProChem** (Elliston, VA) and **Aquatrol** (TX) also blend.
- **Butler Water Corrections** (NJ, 1938) makes patented, non-toxic HVAC and food-service equipment treatments.

On the equipment side, EAI's Vista, CA plant builds RO/UF systems, softeners, and on-site chlorine/ClO2 generators. Aqua Clear (San Diego) supplies membrane systems and membrane chemicals, and Dioxide Pacific engineers ClO2/ozone/UV disinfection.

**End markets & customers.** Commercial HVAC and buildings is the largest end market (about 30%): office and commercial real estate portfolios in NYC and New England, healthcare and education (about 10%), and data centers (about 6%, a stated theme for ProChem and Tower). General manufacturing and food & beverage follow. The utilities division sells mainly to municipal water districts (about 12% municipal drinking water) and agricultural well owners (about 8%).

**Footprint.** Sylmar is strongest in Southern and Northern California (EAI, Aqua Clear, Western Water, the pump/well brands). A Northeast corridor was built from 2024-26 with Clearwater and Artech (CT), Atlantic (RI), Tower (NYC/NJ/PA/CT), Butler (NJ) and ETI (PA). Mid-Atlantic and Southeast coverage comes from ProChem and LaMotte (VA) and R2J (Tampa). Aquatrol, acquired in 2026, adds Texas.

**Financials.** No figures are disclosed. ZoomInfo shows $77.3M, which is consistent with the pre-2026 perimeter.
- **Revenue build-up (estimate):** water treatment service about $64M, external blending about $11M, equipment about $7M, pump/well about $30M, for about $112M.
- **US water treatment revenue (strict):** about $75M.
- **EBITDA (estimate):** about $20M (about 18% margin). This is inferred from the $130M senior facility at typical lower-middle-market leverage (4.5-5.5x on a partly funded facility). Treat it as low confidence.

**M&A strategy.** Sylmar runs a programmatic buy-and-build of founder-owned regional treaters at small-deal multiples. Brands, founders and local names are kept (a "decentralized network"), backed by central finance, procurement and in-house blending (ETI/ProChem) that captures chemical margin. Deal pace has accelerated: 2 in 2024, 5 in 2025 and 4 by mid-2026 (Atlantic, Aquatrol, Butler, Tower). Tower Water (50+ employees) is the largest deal to date and creates a dense NY/NJ/CT position. The McLean Group has named Sylmar among the most active buyers in water.

**Competitive position.** Sylmar is a mid-sized consolidator competing against Chem-Aqua (Diversey), ChemTreat (Veralto), Nalco (Ecolab) and other consolidators such as Vanguard/Veolia-backed platforms. Its edge is local service density, Legionella compliance expertise and a captive blender. It has scale disadvantages versus the majors in R&D and national accounts.

**Risks.**
- Integration risk across roughly 17 small brands.
- Key-person and founder-retention risk at acquired firms.
- Leverage following the $130M facility.
- The non-core, cyclical, capex-heavy well/pump business. It dilutes the "water treatment" story and may be separated at exit.

**Uncertainties.** Actual revenue, EBITDA and headcount; equity investors' economics; the dates of the Aqua Clear and Dioxide Pacific deals; and how much of ETI's volume is intercompany.
